model.name: Site / Campus
model.purpose: Managed physical container for facilities and infrastructure
model.scope_statement: WM-BLT-008 is the managed physical holding of land and/or water, plus associated siteworks, used as the spatial and operational container for facilities, buildings, civil works and site-level infrastructure. Campus is an operational alias for a multi-facility site or site complex under common management, named in ISO 19650-3 as an asset class alongside portfolios and infrastructure networks, not a separate ISO or IFC feature type. The model covers identity, classification, georeference, legal versus operational extent, composition (site complex, site, site section), contained facilities, tenure and party roles, planning controls, lifecycle including temporary construction and brownfield cases, measurement, evidence and standard alignments. It is format-neutral: IFC, GML, JSON, registers and databases are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Defined area of land or water on which construction, retrofit, demolition or other development is undertaken, including operational holdings after construction.
Campus as a commonly managed multi-facility site or disconnected site complex, including university, hospital, corporate, industrial, data-centre and similar campuses.
Site identity, names, postal address, land-title and cadastral references, and governed global identifiers.
Georeference, coordinate reference system, site origin, elevation datum, footprint and body geometry, area and perimeter quantities.
Composition as site complex, site or site section, and containment of facilities, buildings, roads, railways, marine facilities and external spatial elements.
Owner, operator, occupier, rights, restrictions, responsibilities, easements, zoning and development controls such as coverage ratio, floor-area ratio and height limit.
Lifecycle from acquisition and development through operation, trigger events, transfer of ownership, decommissioning and land restoration.
Temporary and secondary construction sites of the work, environmental contamination status, workplace and access constraints at site scale.

Alignment to IfcSite, ISO 6707-1 site, IEC 62264/ISA-95 site, ISO 41011 built environment and real estate, OGC LandInfra land division, INSPIRE cadastral parcels and LADM spatial units without claiming identity with those classes.
out_of_scope: Settlement, city, town or other populated-place identity, which belongs to WM-PLC-005.
Individual facility, building or indoor spatial structure, which belongs to WM-BLT-006 and building-level models.
Cadastral parcel, title, or party-right-spatial-unit legal object as a first-class land-administration entity; those remain LADM/INSPIRE siblings referenced by this model.
Utility, transport or wet-infrastructure network design as a system model, except site-level service connections, easements and rough location.
Climate, weather-normal, occupancy, population, financial valuation and ecological habitat models, except site-local observations used to operate the holding.
Mobile plant, vessels and consumer products; CERCLA vessels are excluded by statute and are not sites.
Project information models, appointments and CDE workflows as such; ISO 19650 processes govern information about the site but are not the site.

boundary_notes.distinction: A settlement is a populated-place container that may include many independently managed sites. A site or campus is a managed holding with an operator, boundary and contained facilities; it is not a town. ISO 19650-3 lists campuses beside individual buildings and infrastructure networks as assets, not as settlements.

ISO 41011 defines a facility as a collection of assets constructed, installed or established to serve an entity's needs, and infrastructure as a system of facilities. OGC LandInfra defines facility as improvements of or on the land, and site as the land or water area where development is undertaken. IFC4.3 allows IfcSite to be decomposed by IfcFacility and IfcBuilding. This model is the container; the facility is the contained improvement.

INSPIRE cadastral parcels are single areas of Earth surface under homogeneous real-property rights and unique ownership, used as locators into national registers. A managed site often spans many parcels, omits some land inside a visual campus, or includes unregistered public land and water. Pset_LandRegistration and LandTitleID bind this model to those legal objects; they do not make the site the parcel.

ISA-95 Site is a physical, geographical or logical grouping determined by the enterprise and used for rough-cut planning. IFC and ISO 6707-1 sites are physical land or water. A logical manufacturing site without a land holding is an alignment target, not a canonical instance of this physical model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: US CERCLA facility and RCRA facility
boundary_notes.distinction: CERCLA defines facility to include any site or area where a hazardous substance has come to be located. RCRA facility can mean all contiguous land and structures under common control. Those statutory facilities are environmental-liability objects that may overlay a managed site; they are not ISO 41011 facilities and must not be merged into WM-BLT-006 without an explicit overlay.

US 29 CFR 5.2 site of the work includes primary construction sites, secondary fabrication sites and adjacent dedicated support sites for wage-determination purposes. That labour-law envelope can be larger or smaller than the permanent campus and is a time-bounded overlay, not a second identity for the land holding.

Place supplies locational and toponymic identity. This model adds managed extent, tenure, contained assets, operator and lifecycle. A named place is not automatically a site; a site should reference its containing place.

sources.title: IfcSite — IFC 4.3.2.0 (IFC4X3_ADD2) official documentation
sources.relevance: Normative spatial-structure class for a defined area of land, possibly covered with water; composition COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL; georeference, containment of facilities and buildings, GlobalId, LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress (latter two deprecated in ADD2).

sources.title: ISO 6707-1:2020 Buildings and civil engineering works — Vocabulary — Part 1: General terms
sources.relevance: Clause 3.1.1.5 defines site as an area of land or water where construction work or other development is undertaken; distinguishes building, civil engineering works, external works/sitework and land.

sources.title: OPC UA Common Object Model: ISA-95 — ISA95EquipmentElementLevelEnum
sources.relevance: Publishes the ISA-95/IEC 62264 role-based equipment hierarchy: enterprise contains sites; a site is a physical, geographical or logical grouping determined by the enterprise and may contain areas, production lines, process cells and production units.

sources.title: ISO 41011:2024 Facility management — Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines facility management, built environment as collection of buildings, external works, infrastructure and other construction works within an area, facility as a collection of assets serving an entity, infrastructure as a system of facilities, real estate as immoveable property including structures, grounds and undeveloped land, workplace, and facility life cycle.

sources.title: INSPIRE Data Specification on Cadastral Parcels — Technical Guidelines
sources.organization: European Commission INSPIRE Maintenance and Implementation Group
sources.relevance: Defines cadastral parcels as single areas of Earth surface under homogeneous real-property rights and unique ownership, with inspireId, nationalCadastralReference, geometry, label, area, reference point and beginLifespanVersion; compatibility with LADM; parcels are locators, not managed campuses.

sources.title: OGC Land and Infrastructure Conceptual Model Standard (LandInfra)
sources.relevance: Clause 4.2.9 repeats ISO 6707-1 site; 4.2.7 defines facility as improvements of or on the land; land division covers administrative jurisdictions, land parcels, easements and condominiums; survey locates facilities on terrain in compliance with interests in land.

sources.title: 42 U.S. Code § 9601 — CERCLA definitions
sources.relevance: Section 101(9) defines facility as any building, structure, installation or any site or area where a hazardous substance has come to be located, excluding consumer products and vessels; this overlays environmental liability on physical holdings.

sources.title: ISO 19152-2:2025 Geographic information — Land Administration Domain Model (LADM) — Part 2: Land registration
sources.relevance: Abstract model of parties, basic administrative units, rights-responsibilities-restrictions, and spatial units including parcels, legal space of buildings, utilities and civil-engineering elements; SpatialUnitGroup can represent grouped land holdings; VersionedObject supports lifespan.

sources.title: ISO 19650-3:2020 Information management using BIM — Part 3: Operational phase of the assets
sources.relevance: Applies information management to assets of all sizes including portfolios of buildings, campuses, infrastructure networks and individual buildings; defines AIM, PIM-to-AIM transfer, trigger events, appointment, continuity of information on ownership transfer, and points to ISO 19650-5 security-minded approach, ISO 55000 and ISO 41011.

sources.title: OGC CityGML 3.0 Conceptual Model Standard
sources.version_or_date: CityGML 3.0 Part 1 Conceptual Model OGC 20-010, approved 2021-09
sources.relevance: Semantic 3D city objects, LandUse, CityObjectGroup and construction/building modules; no Site class; grouping and land-use are the urban-model counterparts of a managed campus, with BIM/IFC interoperability goals.

sources.title: Pset_LandRegistration — IFC 4.3.2.0
sources.relevance: Property set applicable only to IfcSite: LandID and LandTitleID assigned by the statutory registration authority, plus IsPermanentID distinguishing temporary and permanent identities; replacement for deprecated IfcSite.LandTitleNumber.

sources.title: IEC 62264-1:2013 Enterprise-control system integration — Part 1: Models and terminology
sources.version_or_date: IEC 62264-1:2013 (ISO/IEC dual logo, based on ANSI/ISA-95.00.01)
sources.relevance: Normative role-based equipment hierarchy clauses 5.3.2–5.3.4: Enterprise, Site and Area; site used for rough-cut planning and scheduling; dual physical-asset hierarchy distinct from role-based equipment.

sources.title: Pset_SiteCommon — IFC 4.3.2.0
sources.relevance: Common site properties: Reference, BuildableArea, SiteCoverageRatio, FloorAreaRatio, BuildingHeightLimit and TotalArea; notes that perimeter, area and volume are quantities and classification is via IfcClassificationReference.

sources.title: 29 CFR 5.2 — Definitions, including site of the work
sources.relevance: Defines site of the work as primary construction site where the building or work will remain, secondary sites where a significant portion is constructed for specific use, and adjacent dedicated support sites; excludes general manufacturing of products for the public.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a site or campus is identified, named, addressed and typed independently of file format, including master-system, global and Dimension-assigned identifiers.
bundles.rationale: IfcRoot.GlobalId, IfcSite Name/LongName/SiteAddress, Pset_LandRegistration LandID/LandTitleID, INSPIRE inspireId and nationalCadastralReference, and ISA-95 site as an enterprise-determined grouping all require an identity layer before geometry or tenure can be interpreted.

layers.name: Identity registers and names
layers.description: Authoritative identifiers, governed IRIs, Dimension UUIDs, human names and postal addressing for the holding.

findings.name: Canonical and cross-register identifiers
findings.description: A site must carry a master-system identifier from the operator or statutory land register when one exists, a governed global identifier when published, and a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Dates, names and coordinates are not identifiers. IFC4.3 ADD2 deprecates LandTitleNumber on IfcSite in favour of Pset_LandRegistration LandTitleID and LandID, with IsPermanentID distinguishing temporary survey or construction identities.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier for this site, and which register (operator asset register, statutory land register, or other) is the source of truth?
What governed global identifier or IRI is assigned (IFC GlobalId, INSPIRE inspireId, or other persistent IRI), and is it permanent?
What UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it minted versus when was the identity first observed?
Which statutory LandID and LandTitleID values apply, and do they identify one parcel, several parcels, or a title that is not coincident with the operational site?
If operator site codes, cadastral references and BIM GlobalIds disagree, which identifier wins for operations, legal notice and model exchange?

data_elements.name: Master-system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the operator asset register or statutory registration authority that is treated as source of truth for this holding.

data_elements.name: Governed global identifier
data_elements.description: IfcGloballyUniqueId, INSPIRE Identifier or other persistent IRI used for cross-system publication.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or global identifier is available or as a stable local surrogate.

data_elements.name: Statutory land parcel identifier
data_elements.description: Identification number assigned by the statutory registration authority to a land parcel (Pset_LandRegistration.LandID).

data_elements.name: Statutory land title identifier
data_elements.description: Identification number assigned by the statutory registration authority to the title to a land parcel (Pset_LandRegistration.LandTitleID).

data_elements.name: Permanent identity flag
data_elements.description: True if the statutory identity is permanent; false if temporary (construction, survey, pending registration).

data_elements.name: National cadastral reference
data_elements.description: Thematic identifier at national level linking to the national cadastral register or equivalent.

artifacts.name: Identity register extract
artifacts.description: Certified or timestamped extract from the operator register and/or statutory land register showing current identifiers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register document number plus jurisdiction code; never a date alone.

findings.name: Names, long names and postal address
findings.description: IfcSite carries optional Name, LongName, Description and a postal SiteAddress (deprecated in IFC4.3 ADD2 in favour of Pset_Address). Address is for postal and human location, not geodetic placement. A campus often has a public name distinct from legal title and from construction-site designations.

questions.text: What is the public or campus name, the legal/title name, and any construction or project designation currently in force?
What postal address is assigned to the site, and does it locate the whole campus or only a gatehouse, mailroom or one parcel?
Who authorised the current public name, when did it take effect, and which previous names remain as aliases?

data_elements.name: Public name
data_elements.description: Human-facing site or campus name (IfcSite.LongName / Name).

data_elements.name: Legal or title name
data_elements.description: Name used on title, lease or corporate real-estate records.

data_elements.name: Postal address
data_elements.description: Address given to the site for postal purposes.

data_elements.name: Name aliases
data_elements.description: Former, local or multilingual names retained for search and interoperability.

artifacts.name: Addressing authority record
artifacts.description: Postal or municipal addressing record used to validate SiteAddress/Pset_Address.
artifacts.identity_strategy: National addressing identifier if issued, else Dimension UUID of the address object.

layers.name: Site and campus typology
layers.description: Classification of the holding as construction site, operational campus, industrial site, or other type, and IFC composition type.

findings.name: Site versus campus class and composition type
findings.description: ISO 6707-1 and LandInfra define site as land or water where development is undertaken. ISO 19650-3 names campuses as an operational asset class alongside portfolios and infrastructure networks but does not define a Campus feature type. IFC CompositionType interprets COMPLEX as site complex, ELEMENT as site, PARTIAL as site section. Campus is recorded as an operational class of a site or site complex under common management, not as a competing spatial primitive.

questions.text: Is this instance classified as a construction site, operational campus, industrial site, mixed-use holding, or another documented class, and which classification system is used?
Is the IFC composition type COMPLEX (site complex), ELEMENT (site) or PARTIAL (site section), and if campus, is it one ELEMENT or a COMPLEX of disconnected sites?
If called a campus, are member parcels or sites contiguous, and is non-contiguous satellite land in or out of the same campus identity?
What user-defined ObjectType or national building-code classification reference further specialises the site?

data_elements.name: Site class code
data_elements.description: Operational class such as construction-site, campus, industrial-site, marine-holding or mixed-use, stored as a coded value with scheme.

data_elements.name: Composition type
data_elements.description: COMPLEX, ELEMENT or PARTIAL as defined for IfcSite.

data_elements.name: Classification reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a national or industry classification of the site.

data_elements.name: Contiguity flag
data_elements.description: Whether the operational holding occupies a single contiguous land/water body.

artifacts.name: Classification scheme binding
artifacts.description: Record of the classification system and version used to type the site or campus.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Classification system IRI plus version; instance uses site master identifier.

bundles.name: Spatial extent and georeference
bundles.description: Geometry, coordinate reference systems, reference points, elevation datums, operational boundaries and cadastral alignments.
bundles.rationale: IFC requires precise georeferencing via IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem and IfcMapConversion, with IfcSite latitude/longitude/elevation only as approximate WGS84 indication. INSPIRE and LandInfra require survey-grade geometry tied to land division.

layers.name: Coordinate reference and origin
layers.description: CRS, map conversion, site local origin, true north and elevation datum.

findings.name: CRS, site origin and reference point
findings.description: Precise geospatial information shall be derived from project georeferencing entities relating the engineering coordinate system to a real-world CRS. IfcSite RefLatitude, RefLongitude and RefElevation, if asserted, establish the WGS84 point of local (0,0,0) for approximate use and are not a substitute for IfcMapConversion. INSPIRE recommends a reference point especially useful for small-scale portrayal. Observation time of a survey and event time of a legal boundary change are recorded separately.

questions.text: What coordinate reference system, including datum, projection and epoch, is authoritative for this site?
What easting, northing, orthogonal height, scale and rotation define the map conversion from the engineering system to the CRS?
If approximate WGS84 latitude, longitude and elevation are stored on the site, what is their precision and are they consistent with the map conversion?
When was the georeference surveyed (event time) and when was it ingested into this model (observation time)?

data_elements.name: CRS identifier
data_elements.description: EPSG code, WKT or named CRS for the site engineering-to-world mapping.

data_elements.name: Map conversion parameters
data_elements.description: Parameters mapping the project engineering coordinate system to the geographic or map CRS.

data_elements.name: Reference latitude
data_elements.description: World latitude at the site reference point in WGS84, degrees-minutes-seconds to optional millionths.

data_elements.name: Reference longitude
data_elements.description: World longitude at the site reference point in WGS84.

data_elements.name: Reference elevation
data_elements.description: Datum elevation of the site origin relative to the local height datum.

data_elements.name: Reference point geometry
data_elements.description: INSPIRE-style reference point used for portrayal and locators when full polygon display is impractical.

data_elements.name: Survey event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the survey or legal measurement event, with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Ingestion observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the georeference was recorded in this model.

artifacts.name: Georeferencing report
artifacts.description: Survey or BIM-GIS georeferencing report stating CRS, conversion parameters, control points and residuals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Survey job identifier plus revision; control-point marks use statutory or survey-network IDs.

layers.name: Operational extent and cadastral alignment
layers.description: Legal parcel geometry versus managed operational boundary, including water, air and subsurface interests.

findings.name: Operational and legal boundaries
findings.description: IfcSite footprint may be a 2D curve set with inner boundaries; body geometry may be solid or surface. INSPIRE parcels should form a partition of national territory except unregistered government land. A campus fence line, security perimeter or operational envelope often diverges from cadastral lines, and may include water. LandInfra also covers subsurface and terrain.

questions.text: What geometry represents the operational site or campus envelope, in which CRS, and at which level of detail?
What cadastral or title geometries are bound to this site, and where do they differ from the operational envelope?
Does the managed holding include air rights, subsurface strata or water column, and how is vertical extent recorded?
Which holes, public roads, third-party inholdings or water bodies are excluded from the operational site?

data_elements.name: Operational envelope geometry
data_elements.description: Footprint and optional body of the managed site, possibly with inner boundaries.

data_elements.name: Legal parcel geometries
data_elements.description: Cadastral or title polygons associated with the site.

data_elements.name: Surface relation
data_elements.description: LADM surface relation: above, on, or below the surface.

data_elements.name: Gross site area
data_elements.description: Gross horizontal area from Qto_SiteBaseQuantities.GrossArea.

data_elements.name: Gross perimeter
data_elements.description: Perimeter of the site boundary from Qto_SiteBaseQuantities.GrossPerimeter.

artifacts.name: Site boundary survey
artifacts.description: Cadastral or engineering survey of operational and legal boundaries, including control and exclusion polygons.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Survey plan number issued by licensed surveyor or cadastre; revision identifier required.

findings.name: Cadastral and land-division alignment
findings.description: A site is aligned to, not identical with, INSPIRE CadastralParcel, LADM LA_SpatialUnit / LA_SpatialUnitGroup, and LandInfra land parcels, easements and condominiums. National cadastral references must keep the link to the national register. Grouping of spatial units with shared rights is a LADM SpatialUnitGroup pattern that can represent a multi-parcel campus without collapsing parcels.

questions.text: Which cadastral parcels, basic property units or SpatialUnit identifiers are bound to this site, and is the binding complete?
Is the campus represented as a LADM SpatialUnitGroup of parcels, and what grouping criterion (common title, common operator, common security perimeter) is used?
If some occupied land is unregistered, customary or informal, how is that spatial unit recorded without claiming cadastral completeness?
Are condominium, strata or air-right units present, and do they fragment the site's vertical or horizontal management?

data_elements.name: Bound parcel identifiers
data_elements.description: National cadastral references or LADM suIDs associated with the site.

data_elements.name: Spatial unit group identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a LADM SpatialUnitGroup used for a multi-parcel campus.

data_elements.name: INSPIRE identifier
data_elements.description: inspireId of cadastral objects used as locators, not as the site identity itself.

data_elements.name: Cadastral lifespan begin
data_elements.description: Date-time the spatial object was inserted or changed in the cadastral source.

artifacts.name: Cadastral register extract
artifacts.description: Official parcel, zoning overlay and easement extract from the national or state cadastre.
artifacts.identity_strategy: nationalCadastralReference plus extract request identifier; inspireId where published.

bundles.name: Composition and containment
bundles.description: How a site complex, site and site section nest, and which facilities, buildings and siteworks they contain or only reference.
bundles.rationale: IFC spatial decomposition and containment, ISA-95 enterprise-site-area hierarchy, and ISO 41011 built-environment/facility/infrastructure stacking are the three primary composition stories and they do not coincide.

layers.name: IFC spatial structure and contained assets
layers.description: Site complex, site, site section, and contained or referenced products including facilities and siteworks.

findings.name: Site complex, site, section and contained assets
findings.description: A project may span several connected or disconnected sites. IfcSite.IsDecomposedBy may reference other IfcSite instances, IfcBuilding, IfcFacility, IfcBridge, IfcMarineFacility, IfcRailway, IfcRoad, IfcExternalSpatialElement or IfcSpace. Elements such as fences or shear walls are contained via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure rather than aggregation. LandInfra treats facilities as improvements on the land and siteworks as associated landscape or construction works.

questions.text: Does this site belong to a site complex, and which sibling sites are connected or disconnected members of that complex?
Which facilities, buildings and civil works are aggregated under this site, and which product elements are merely contained or referenced?
How is the site decomposed into sections or areas, and is that decomposition spatial, operational or both?
Which external works, landscape, roads, fences and other siteworks are part of the site rather than of a child facility?
Which elements (shared utilities, roads, security fences) are referenced by more than one spatial structure and how is primary containment chosen?

data_elements.name: Parent site or complex identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the relating IfcSite with higher CompositionType when this instance is a part.

data_elements.name: Child site or section identifiers
data_elements.description: Sites or sections aggregated by this instance.

data_elements.name: Contained facility identifiers
data_elements.description: WM-BLT-006 and IFC IfcFacility/IfcBuilding instances decomposed from this site.

data_elements.name: Contained product element identifiers
data_elements.description: Non-spatial products contained in the site (fences, tanks, site furniture).

data_elements.name: Referenced element identifiers
data_elements.description: Products referenced in this spatial structure but primarily contained elsewhere.

artifacts.name: Spatial structure graph
artifacts.description: Canonical decomposition and containment graph of the site complex, sites, sections, facilities and contained elements.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Rooted at the site master identifier; edge typed as aggregates, contains or references.

layers.name: Enterprise role-based site
layers.description: ISA-95/IEC 62264 site as a planning grouping that may or may not coincide with the land holding.

findings.name: Role-based site in the enterprise hierarchy
findings.description: IEC 62264 Site is determined by the enterprise, used for rough-cut planning, and may be physical, geographical or logical. Area is determined by the site. This alignment records the manufacturing or operations hierarchy without replacing the land model. A logical site with no geometry is marked as an alignment instance, not a canonical physical site.

questions.text: Which enterprise identity determines this ISA-95 site, and is the grouping physical, geographical or logical?
Which areas, work centres and work units are children of this site in the role-based equipment hierarchy?
If the ISA-95 site is logical, which physical WM-BLT-008 holdings does it overlay, and is a geometry-less site allowed as a canonical instance?

data_elements.name: ISA-95 site identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the role-based equipment hierarchy site.

data_elements.name: Grouping kind
data_elements.description: physical, geographical or logical as allowed by ISA-95.

data_elements.name: Enterprise identifier
data_elements.description: Parent enterprise in the role-based hierarchy.

data_elements.name: Child area identifiers
data_elements.description: ISA-95 areas determined by this site.

findings.inline_only_rationale: ISA-95 hierarchy membership is reference data to enterprise-control systems; no distinctive site artifact is required beyond the typed identifiers and grouping kind.

bundles.name: Tenure, authority and constraints
bundles.description: Who owns, operates and regulates the holding, which rights and easements apply, and which planning controls limit development.
bundles.rationale: LADM party-RRR-spatial unit, IFC owner history and land registration properties, LandInfra interests in land, and Pset_SiteCommon development controls jointly define authority over a site.

layers.name: Tenure and parties
layers.description: Title, leases, owner, operator, occupier and LADM rights, restrictions and responsibilities.

findings.name: Title, rights, owner and operator
findings.description: LADM models people-to-land as party, RRR and spatial unit. ISO 41011 distinguishes real estate (immoveable property including grounds) from facility management as the organisational function integrating people, place and process. ISO 19650-3 requires continuity of the asset information model when an asset transfers from one owner to another. Owner, operator and occupier are distinct roles and may be many-to-one on a campus.

questions.text: Who is the legal owner or owners of the land and of the improvements, and under which title or lease instruments?
Who is the site or campus operator, and is facility management insourced, outsourced or co-sourced?
Which rights, restrictions and responsibilities (including informal or customary) bind parties to this holding?
If ownership or operatorship transferred, when did the event occur, and was the asset information model transferred with it?

data_elements.name: Owner party identifiers
data_elements.description: Parties holding ownership or equivalent registered interest.

data_elements.name: Operator party identifier
data_elements.description: Party responsible for operating the site or campus.

data_elements.name: Rights, restrictions and responsibilities
data_elements.description: LADM RRR records bound to the site's spatial units.

data_elements.name: IFC owner history
data_elements.description: Owning actor, application and change capture for the IFC projection of the site object.

artifacts.name: Title or lease instrument
artifacts.description: Deed, title register extract, lease or concession that evidences ownership or occupation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: LandTitleID or instrument number from the statutory register; date is metadata not identity.

layers.name: Planning controls and encumbrances
layers.description: Zoning, buildable area, coverage, floor-area ratio, height limits, easements and other interests in land.

findings.name: Development controls and easements
findings.description: Pset_SiteCommon records BuildableArea, SiteCoverageRatio, FloorAreaRatio, BuildingHeightLimit and TotalArea according to local building codes. LandInfra covers easements, SuperficieObject and condominium interests that legally protect or constrain facilities even when utility design is out of scope. Planning authority is distinct from land owner.

questions.text: Which planning or building-code authority sets development controls for this site, and which zoning or plan-unit designations apply?
What are the current buildable area, site coverage ratio, floor-area ratio, height limit and total planned area?
Which easements, rights of way, superficie or other interests in land encumber the site, and which facilities do they protect or restrict?
If local code, campus master plan and recorded easements conflict, which constraint is binding for a proposed development?

data_elements.name: Buildable area
data_elements.description: Maximum site utilisation area according to local building codes.

data_elements.name: Site coverage ratio
data_elements.description: Maximum utilisation ratio TotalArea/BuildableArea.

data_elements.name: Floor area ratio
data_elements.description: Maximum ratio of all floor areas to buildable area.

data_elements.name: Building height limit
data_elements.description: Allowed maximum height of buildings on this site according to local codes.

data_elements.name: Total planned area
data_elements.description: Total planned area for programming the site space.

data_elements.name: Easements and interests in land
data_elements.description: Easements, superficie and similar LandInfra interests.

artifacts.name: Planning permit or campus master plan
artifacts.description: Zoning designation, master plan or building-permit envelope that states development controls.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Permit or plan identifier issued by the planning authority.

artifacts.name: Easement or right-of-way instrument
artifacts.description: Recorded interest in land with geometry where available.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Statutory instrument number; geometry uses cadastral or survey identity.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, operations and environment
bundles.description: States of the holding from acquisition through operation, construction overlays, contamination and access.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19650-3 defines operational trigger events, AIM aggregation and ownership-transfer information continuity, including campuses. ISO 41011 defines facility life cycle. Construction site-of-the-work and CERCLA contamination are distinct overlays.

layers.name: Lifecycle states and trigger events
layers.description: Permanent holding lifecycle versus temporary construction envelope and AIM/PIM information states.

findings.name: Operational lifecycle and trigger events
findings.description: ISO 19650-3 applies to campuses and other assets through scheduled trigger events (maintenance, estate reviews) and unscheduled events (breakdowns, accidents, floods), plus acquisition from an existing owner. PIM contributes to AIM at the start of operation; AIM contributes to PIM at the start of a delivery phase. Continuity of information on owner transfer is required. Facility life cycle and post-occupancy evaluation are ISO 41011 concepts.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle state of the holding (planned, under construction, operational, mothballed, decommissioning, restored), and when did that state begin?
Which ISO 19650-3 trigger events are scheduled or have occurred, and did they open a delivery-phase PIM or an operational AIM update?
Where are the current asset information model and any contributing project information models, and what was transferred at points A and B?
If the site is being decommissioned, what restoration, residual-risk and information-archive obligations remain?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Coded state of the managed holding.

data_elements.name: State start time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 start of the current lifecycle state.

data_elements.name: Trigger events
data_elements.description: Scheduled or unscheduled operational trigger events.

data_elements.name: Asset information model locator
data_elements.description: Reference to the AIM that governs operational information for this campus or site.

artifacts.name: AIM handover or aggregation record
artifacts.description: Record of PIM-to-AIM or owner-to-owner information transfer for the site or campus.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Appointment or handover identifier from the appointing party; site master identifier as subject.

findings.name: Construction site of the work and temporary holdings
findings.description: ISO 6707-1 site is where construction or other development is undertaken. 29 CFR 5.2 extends site of the work to secondary fabrication sites and adjacent dedicated support sites for wage law. Pset_LandRegistration.IsPermanentID distinguishes temporary identities. A construction envelope may exist only for a duration and must not silently replace the permanent campus identity.

questions.text: Is this instance a permanent holding, a time-bounded construction site of the work, or a secondary/support site, and what are its start and planned end times?
Which secondary construction or adjacent support sites are linked to the primary site of the work, and are they inside the permanent campus?
Does a labour-law site-of-the-work envelope differ from the operational campus, and which activities are excluded as general manufacturing?

data_elements.name: Holding kind
data_elements.description: permanent, primary-construction, secondary-construction or adjacent-support.

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 start of the construction or temporary holding.

data_elements.name: Valid to
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 planned or actual end of the temporary holding.

data_elements.name: Linked permanent site identifier
data_elements.description: Permanent campus or site that a temporary construction envelope overlays.

artifacts.name: Construction site notice or wage determination attachment
artifacts.description: Notice identifying primary, secondary and support sites of the work.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Contract or project identifier plus labour-agency determination number.

layers.name: Environmental status and access
layers.description: Contamination overlays, workplace safety of the physical location, and access exceptions.

findings.name: Contamination and environmental status
findings.description: CERCLA facility includes any site or area where a hazardous substance has come to be located. That statutory overlay can cover part of a campus, a wider plume, or land with no current operator. It must be recorded as environmental status and responsible-party information, not used to rename the site as a facility in the ISO 41011 sense.

questions.text: Is any part of this holding a known or suspected contaminated site or CERCLA/RCRA facility, and what is the regulatory list status?
Who are the potentially responsible or permitted parties for contamination, and how do they relate to the land owner and site operator?
What removal or remedial actions are active, and how do they constrain construction, occupancy or transfer of the site?

data_elements.name: Contamination status
data_elements.description: Coded environmental overlay status, including none-known, suspected, listed, remediating, closed.

data_elements.name: CERCLA facility overlay flag
data_elements.description: True if a CERCLA facility definition currently overlays this holding.

data_elements.name: Affected geometry
data_elements.description: Portion of the site or off-site plume associated with the overlay.

artifacts.name: Environmental site assessment or listing record
artifacts.description: Phase I/II assessment, NPL or equivalent listing, or remediation decision document.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Regulatory site identifier (for example EPA ID) if assigned; else assessment report number.

findings.name: Access, security and workplace
findings.description: ISO 41011 locates facility management in the built environment with the purpose of safe workplaces. ISO 19650-3 points to ISO 19650-5 for a security-minded approach to asset information. Site-scale access (gates, perimeters, visitor regimes) is distinct from indoor access control. Public cadastral geometry may need redaction for sensitive campuses.

questions.text: What is the default physical access regime for this site (public, controlled, restricted, classified), and which perimeters and gates enforce it?
Which site information (geometry, occupancy, utilities) is security-sensitive under ISO 19650-5 principles, and who may read it?
Is the entire campus a single workplace/establishment or are multiple workplaces recorded, and what exceptions exist for public realm?
What emergency-access exceptions (fire, medical, environmental response) override the default access rule?

data_elements.name: Access regime
data_elements.description: Default physical access classification of the site.

data_elements.name: Information sensitivity labels
data_elements.description: Security-minded labels for site information elements.

data_elements.name: Workplace identifiers
data_elements.description: ISO 41011 workplaces or establishments mapped onto the site.

artifacts.name: Site access and security-minded information policy
artifacts.description: Policy stating physical access, information redaction and emergency exceptions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier and version issued by the site operator.

bundles.name: Measurement, evidence and interoperability
bundles.description: Quantities, survey quality, standard mappings, conflicts and information retention.
bundles.rationale: IFC quantities and property sets, INSPIRE lifespan metadata, LADM versioned objects, CityGML grouping, and ISO 19650 archive rules are the evidence and interoperability surface.

layers.name: Quantities and survey quality
layers.description: Measured and planned site quantities and the quality of geometric evidence.

findings.name: Site quantities and evidence quality
findings.description: Qto_SiteBaseQuantities provide GrossPerimeter and GrossArea. Pset_SiteCommon TotalArea is planned/programmed area and may differ from measured GrossArea. LandInfra relies on survey observations. Quality must state method, accuracy and whether values are measured, calculated or regulatory maxima.

questions.text: What are the measured gross area, perimeter and optional volume, in which units, and by which method?
How does planned TotalArea and BuildableArea differ from measured GrossArea, and which value is used for which decision?
What positional accuracy, completeness and logical consistency are claimed for the site geometry, and what evidence supports the claim?
Which validation rules failed or passed (CRS consistency, parcel coverage, FAR not exceeded, identifier uniqueness)?

data_elements.name: Measured gross area
data_elements.description: Measured horizontal gross area of the site.

data_elements.name: Measured gross perimeter
data_elements.description: Measured perimeter of the site boundary.

data_elements.name: Quantity method
data_elements.description: measured, calculated or regulatory-maximum.

data_elements.name: Positional accuracy
data_elements.description: Stated accuracy of site geometry.

artifacts.name: Quantity take-off and validation record
artifacts.description: Record of measured versus planned quantities and validation outcomes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Take-off run identifier plus site master identifier.

layers.name: Standard mappings and retention
layers.description: Alignments to IFC, CityGML, LandInfra, LADM/INSPIRE, ISA-95 and ISO 19650 retention.

findings.name: Standard mappings, conflicts and information retention
findings.description: CityGML has no Site class; CityObjectGroup and LandUse are the urban grouping and land-cover counterparts. IFC IfcSite is the BIM counterpart. LandInfra Facility is the improvement, not the land. ISO 19650-3 requires storing information for archive and audit and transferring AIM on ownership change. Security-minded redaction may prevent publishing full geometry. These are alignments, not claimed conformance of any instance.

questions.text: Which IfcSite GlobalId, composition type and georeferencing mode map this instance, and is LandTitleNumber avoided in IFC4.3 ADD2 export?
If published into a city model, is the campus a CityObjectGroup, a LandUse object, both, or unmapped, and at which LOD?
Which standards is this instance claimed to conform to, and what evidence exists versus mere alignment?
How long are site geometry, title extracts, AIM snapshots and access logs retained, and what is deleted or anonymised on decommission?

data_elements.name: IFC GlobalId
data_elements.description: IfcGloballyUniqueId of the mapped IfcSite.

data_elements.name: CityGML object identifiers
data_elements.description: Identifiers of CityObjectGroup, LandUse or other city objects mapping this site.

data_elements.name: Conformance claims
data_elements.description: Explicit conformance statements with evidence, distinct from alignment.

data_elements.name: Retention policy identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the information retention and deletion policy for this site.

artifacts.name: Interoperability mapping record
artifacts.description: Record of IFC, CityGML, LandInfra, LADM/INSPIRE and ISA-95 identifiers and whether each is alignment or evidenced conformance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Site master identifier plus mapping-set version.

artifacts.name: AGENTS.md bootstrap contract
artifacts.description: Mandatory agent bootstrap describing name, type, specification, storage type, interface and processes URLs for this site context, independent of MongoDB, Git or MCP storage.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Fixed filename AGENTS.md at the context root; content identifies the site by master-system identifier.

functions.name: Register site or campus
functions.description: Create a governed site/campus record with master-system identifier, Dimension UUID, class and composition type.
outputs: site record with master_system_id and dimension_uuid
preconditions: Caller is authorised to create holdings
effects: A new WM-BLT-008 instance exists in lifecycle state planned or as declared
Identifiers are reserved in the identity register

functions.name: Georeference site
functions.description: Bind CRS, map conversion and optional WGS84 reference point, recording survey event time and ingestion time separately.
preconditions: Survey or conversion parameters are internally consistent
effects: Authoritative CRS mapping is stored
Approximate WGS84 values are flagged as non-authoritative if map conversion exists

functions.name: Compose site structure
functions.description: Set COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL composition and parent/child site relations, including disconnected members of a campus complex.
preconditions: Composition types respect IFC COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL stacking
effects: Aggregation edges are written
Campus aggregation mode is recorded

functions.name: Bind contained facility
functions.description: Aggregate or contain a facility, building or sitework under the site, or record a reference-only relationship.
preconditions: Target is not a settlement or cadastral parcel
effects: WM-BLT-006 or IFC facility/building/sitework is linked
Primary container is unique for contains/aggregates

functions.name: Bind cadastral units
functions.description: Associate LandID, LandTitleID, INSPIRE locators or LADM spatial units and optional SpatialUnitGroup without collapsing legal parcels.
preconditions: Statutory identifiers are well-formed for the jurisdiction
effects: Legal substrate is referenced
Operational geometry remains independent

functions.name: Assign party roles
functions.description: Record owner, operator, occupier and LADM RRR, and optionally transfer AIM on ownership change.
preconditions: Parties are identified in a party register
effects: Ownership and operatorship are current
ISO 19650-3 continuity obligation is either fulfilled or recorded as a gap

functions.name: Transition lifecycle state
functions.description: Move the holding through planned, construction, operational, mothballed, decommissioning or restored states, opening PIM or AIM updates on trigger events.
preconditions: Effective time is RFC 3339 with offset or Z
effects: State start time is recorded
Temporary construction overlays do not overwrite permanent identity

functions.name: Record environmental status
functions.description: Attach a contamination or statutory-facility overlay, affected geometry and responsible parties.
preconditions: Overlay is not used to replace site or facility class
effects: CERCLA/RCRA or equivalent overlay is queryable
Occupancy and transfer constraints are visible

functions.name: Compute and validate site quantities
functions.description: Derive or import GrossArea, GrossPerimeter, planned TotalArea and development-control ratios, then validate against CRS and FAR/coverage limits.
effects: Measured versus planned values are distinguished
Failed rules block non-exception updates

functions.name: Publish interoperability mapping
functions.description: Write IFC, CityGML, LandInfra, LADM/INSPIRE and ISA-95 identifiers and state whether each is alignment or evidenced conformance.
preconditions: Deprecated IfcSite.LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress are not exported on IFC4.3 ADD2
effects: Mappings are queryable
Unsubstantiated conformance claims are refused

composition.purpose: A site or campus contains facilities as improvements of or on the land; IFC4.3 allows IfcSite to decompose to IfcFacility and IfcBuilding.
A settlement may contain many sites; the site references its containing populated place without inheriting settlement identity.
Place supplies locational and toponymic context; the site adds managed extent, operator and contained assets.
Primary BIM spatial-structure alignment for land area, georeference, composition type and containment.
Enterprise role-based planning hierarchy; logical sites remain overlays on physical holdings.
Legal land units and titles are the cadastral substrate; a campus may group them as a SpatialUnitGroup.

composition.target: OGC LandInfra Facility and land division
composition.purpose: LandInfra site is the land/water area; facility is the improvement; land division and easements bind interests in land.
Built environment is the collection of buildings, external works and infrastructure within an area; real estate is the immoveable property including grounds.
CityGML has no Site class; grouping and land-use objects are the urban-model counterparts.
Operational information about the campus or site lives in an AIM governed by trigger events and appointments, not in the spatial object itself.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the operator or land-owner organisation package that is source of truth for master-system site identifiers.
Declare the statutory land-registration package or jurisdiction whose LandID/LandTitleID values may be bound.
Declare the geospatial CRS package and the BIM/AIM packages allowed to write geometry and lifecycle state.
Separate the settlement/place package from this site package so populated-place identity cannot be stored as a site.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable site namespace keyed by master-system identifier, with child fragments for sections, overlays (construction, contamination, wage-law) and mappings (ifc, inspire, isa95). Do not use dates, campus marketing names or coordinates as namespace roots. IRIs, when published, should follow the governed identifier of the Dimension and must not collide with cadastral parcel IRIs.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical site identity is master-system identifier, then governed IRI/GlobalId, then Dimension UUID/ULID; names and dates never canonicalize.
Canonical geometry is the operational envelope in the declared CRS; WGS84 RefLatitude/RefLongitude/RefElevation are derived or approximate and lose if they conflict with map conversion.
Canonical composition type is COMPLEX, ELEMENT or PARTIAL; campus is a class of ELEMENT or COMPLEX, not a fourth composition type.
Cadastral parcels remain referenced objects; do not merge multi-parcel geometry into a single legal parcel identifier.
patch_rules: Patches must be scoped to identity, geometry, composition, tenure, lifecycle, overlay or mapping bundles and must record actor, event time and ingestion time.
Geometry patches require a survey or derived-from reference and may not silently replace legal parcel geometry.
Lifecycle patches may not reuse a temporary construction identity as the permanent site identifier.
Deprecated IFC attributes LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress must be patched into Pset_LandRegistration and Pset_Address on IFC4.3 ADD2 export.
compatibility_rules: Readers must accept both IFC2x3-style LandTitleNumber and IFC4.3 Pset_LandRegistration without treating them as two sites.
ISA-95 logical sites may overlay but must not replace physical geometry.
CityGML LandUse or CityObjectGroup mappings are optional and many-to-one.
A CERCLA facility overlay sharing a name with the campus is not a duplicate WM-BLT-008 record.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier from the operator register or statutory land register.
Governed global identifier or IRI (IfcGloballyUniqueId, INSPIRE inspireId).
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record event time (survey, transfer, trigger, legal change) and observation/ingestion time separately whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (surveys, permits, title extracts, AIM handovers, environmental assessments) use issuer-assigned document or instrument numbers plus revision; site master identifier is the subject, not the serial.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store a content hash of serial artifacts and the geometry they authorise; reject unsigned replacement of boundary, title or environmental listing artifacts.

policies: Physical site records default to operator-controlled access; cadastral extracts follow the originating jurisdiction's disclosure law.
Security-minded redaction of gates, utilities and occupancy applies to sensitive campuses before any public city-model publication.
Temporary construction and contamination overlays expire or close by explicit state change; they are never deleted silently while legal obligations remain.
Ownership transfer must attempt AIM continuity per ISO 19650-3; failure is recorded as a governed gap, not ignored.

read: Any authenticated agent with site.read may read non-sensitive identity, class and public address.
Geometry, utilities, occupancy and security perimeters require site.read.geometry or higher.
Title instruments and environmental listings follow legal-privilege scopes.
create: site.create is limited to owner, operator or appointed information manager.
Creation requires master-system identifier or an explicit temporary IsPermanentID=false.
Creation of a campus COMPLEX requires member ELEMENT identities.
update: Geometry updates require surveyor or geospatial-steward role and a georeferencing report.
Lifecycle updates require operator or appointing party and an RFC 3339 effective time.
delete: Hard delete is forbidden while statutory, contamination or AIM archive obligations exist.
Logical retirement sets lifecycle state restored or decommissioned and retains identifiers.
Temporary construction identities may be closed at valid_to but remain historically queryable.

roles.name: Site owner
responsibilities: Hold or evidence legal title or equivalent interest
Authorise operatorship and AIM transfer on sale

roles.name: Site operator / facility manager
responsibilities: Maintain operational envelope, access regime and contained-facility graph

roles.name: Land registrar / cadastral authority
responsibilities: Issue LandID and LandTitleID or national cadastral references
Publish parcel geometry and lifespan versions

roles.name: Planning authority
responsibilities: Set zoning, coverage, FAR and height controls
Issue permits that bind BuildableArea and related constraints

roles.name: Environmental regulator
responsibilities: Constrain occupancy and transfer where required

roles.name: Information manager
responsibilities: Keep AGENTS.md, AIM locators and interoperability mappings current
Enforce identifier priority, timestamps and security-minded redaction

access.default_rule: Deny public write; allow authenticated read of non-sensitive identity and public address; require explicit scopes for geometry, tenure, environment and security perimeters.
exceptions: Emergency responders may read access-regime, gate and affected-geometry under recorded emergency-access exceptions.
Statutory cadastral publication may disclose parcel geometry even when campus security policy would redact operational fences.
Temporary construction wage-law envelopes may be disclosed to labour authorities without granting full AIM access.
audit_requirements: Log create, update, delete, overlay and mapping changes with actor, event time and ingestion time.
Log reads of security-sensitive geometry and environmental listings.
Retain audit logs at least as long as the AIM archive obligation for the site.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any other site context file.
Resolve master-system identifier and CRS from the specification-linked site record before interpreting geometry or contained facilities.
Apply security-minded access in AGENTS.md processes before publishing CityGML, IFC or cadastral extracts.

coverage.claim: This result defines a defensible, format-neutral operating surface for a managed physical site or campus as a container of facilities and infrastructure, grounded in IFC IfcSite, ISO 6707-1, ISO 19650-3 (which names campuses), ISO 41011 built environment/real estate, IEC 62264/ISA-95 site, OGC LandInfra land division, INSPIRE cadastral parcels and LADM spatial units. It does not claim a universal Campus feature type or statutory conformance of any instance.

checklist.notes: Master-system, GlobalId/inspireId, Dimension UUID, LandID/LandTitleID and IsPermanentID are modelled; dates are excluded as identifiers.
ISO 19650-3 trigger events and AIM/PIM, ISO 41011 facility life cycle, temporary construction holdings and decommission/restoration are included.
Contains facilities, references settlement/place and cadastral units, overlays ISA-95, CERCLA and wage-law envelopes.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion time, cadastral beginLifespanVersion, construction valid_from/valid_to and state_began_at.
OwnerHistory, surveyor, register extracts, name authority and AIM handover records.
LADM party-RRR, distinct owner/operator/occupier, ISO 19650-3 transfer continuity.
CRS consistency, parcel coverage, FAR/coverage rules, identifier uniqueness and alignment-versus-conformance flags.
Site-scale access regime, security-minded information labels, workplace mapping and emergency exceptions; indoor ACS left to facility models.
AIM archive, logical retirement, overlay expiry and prohibition on silent delete while legal obligations remain.
Explicit ALIGN/REFERENCE maps to IFC, CityGML, LandInfra, INSPIRE/LADM, ISA-95 and ISO 41011, with documented conflicts.
Operational versus legal geometry, vertical interests, exclusions and georeferencing.
Parcels remain siblings; SpatialUnitGroup may represent a multi-parcel campus.
CERCLA facility overlay is modelled as status, not as the site or ISO facility class.
Campus is an operational class of a site or site complex named by ISO 19650-3; no dedicated ISO/IFC Campus entity exists.
29 CFR 5.2 site of the work is a time-bounded overlay on ISO 6707-1/IFC permanent holdings.

known_omissions: No primary international feature type named Campus; higher-education, hospital and data-centre campus information models were not adopted as canonical classes.
Military installation and NATO/DoD site schemas were not retrieved as primary sources.
OSHA establishment combining nearby locations was only partially retrieved because eCFR blocked a full fetch; workplace mapping is therefore thinner than access policy.
Customary and informal tenure is acknowledged via LADM but not operationalised with a regional code list.
3D/4D cadastral air rights and subsurface volumes lack a single implementable geometry profile in this model.
Wet-infrastructure networks are out of LandInfra's initial release and remain out of this site model except as easements.
Biodiversity, occupancy, valuation (LADM Part 4) and climate normals are sibling models.
Seveso/IED, UK COMAH and other non-US contamination regimes are not cited as primary overlays.
IFC Pset_SiteWeather exists but weather is treated as observation, not as a climate sibling, and was not expanded.
conflicts: IEC 62264/ISA-95 Site may be logical; ISO 6707-1 and IfcSite are physical land or water.
CERCLA 'facility' includes 'any site or area'; ISO 41011 'facility' is a collection of assets; Vercy WM-BLT-006 is the latter.
INSPIRE cadastral parcel (homogeneous unique ownership) often does not coincide with a multi-parcel or multi-owner campus.
IfcSite.RefLatitude/RefLongitude/RefElevation are approximate WGS84; IfcMapConversion is authoritative and may disagree.
IFC4.3 ADD2 deprecates LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress that remain in widespread IFC2x3/IFC4 data.
29 CFR 5.2 site of the work can include off-campus secondary fabrication sites that are not part of the permanent holding.
CityGML LandUse is land cover/use, not a managed operator holding; grouping via CityObjectGroup is not equivalent to IfcSite.
regional_assumptions: Cadastral identifier schemes, title versus deeds systems, and whether government land is registered, are jurisdiction-specific.
INSPIRE ETRS89 practices apply in the EU; WGS84 approximate points are common in BIM and may be inappropriate for cadastral use.
CERCLA/RCRA overlays are United States law; other jurisdictions need local contaminated-land instruments.
Davis-Bacon site of the work is United States labour law; other public-works wage envelopes will differ.
Campus as an English operational term is common in ISO 19650-3 examples but is not a translated statutory class.
Common-law versus civil-law treatment of easements, superficie and condominium will change RRR cardinality.
adversarial_checks: A site can exist without a cadastral parcel (unregistered public land, water, informal occupation); requiring LandTitleID would falsely exclude those holdings.
A campus can be non-contiguous (satellite teaching hospitals, split data-centre halls); forcing a single polygon would corrupt identity.
A construction site of the work can exist with IsPermanentID=false and no land title; collapsing it into the permanent campus would break wage-law and safety records.
A company town can be both settlement and site; storing it only as WM-BLT-008 would hide populated-place semantics.
A logical ISA-95 site with no geometry must not satisfy canonical physical-site validation.
Multiple operators on one parcel (business park, hospital-plus-university) require many operator roles, not duplicate parcel identities.
Air-rights or subsurface campuses over railways would fail a 2D fence-line-only model.
A CERCLA plume extending off-site must not enlarge the managed campus identity.
Publishing full IfcSite geometry for a secure campus would violate ISO 19650-5 security-minded practice even if CityGML interoperability encourages it.
